Question:
Consider the function

\[f(x) = |\lfloor x \rfloor| - |\lfloor 1 - x \rfloor|\]

Its graph is symmetric about which of the following? (Here \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) is the greatest integer not exceeding \(x.\))
Solution:
Replacing \(x\) with \(1-x\) interchanges the two terms of the function:
\[
f(1-x)=|\lfloor1-x\rfloor|-|\lfloor x\rfloor|=-f(x).
\]
Thus whenever \((x,y)\) is on the graph, so is \((1-x,-y)\). Their midpoint is always \((1/2,0)\), which proves symmetry about \(\boxed{(1/2,0)}\), choice D.

For completeness, \(f(-1)=-1\), \(f(0)=-1\), and \(f(1)=f(2)=1\) rule out the other four symmetries. The values at \(1\) and \(-1\) rule out the \(y\)-axis; the values at \(0\) and \(2\) rule out the line \(x=1\); and the nonzero values at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) rule out those points as centers on the \(x\)-axis.
